hearth.wild.ask.hermitage: Why do you live out here?
hearth.wild.ask.monastery: What do the brothers do up here?
hearth.wild.ask.farmstead: Is it a hard life up here?
hearth.wild.about.hospice.0: We do. The brothers of the pass. Whoever comes over the saddle gets a bowl and a bench, and nobody asks his name.
hearth.wild.about.hospice.1: When the cloud comes down we ring the bell, so a man lost up there can walk toward it. Most nights it brings someone in.
hearth.wild.about.hospice.2: Every spring we find the ones who did not hear it. Say a prayer for them on your way down.
hearth.wild.about.inn.0: Carters say the bridge downriver is half rotten. And there's a band in the woods past the second milestone, so keep your purse quiet.
hearth.wild.about.inn.1: A day's walk to the next roof either way. That's why we're here, and why the beer costs what it costs.
hearth.wild.about.inn.2: A lord's man came through last week asking after a red-haired fellow. Paid well for an answer, too. We hadn't one.
hearth.wild.about.toll_gate.0: The lord's, and the bridge's. Somebody has to pay for the timber when the spring flood takes another span.
hearth.wild.about.toll_gate.1: Carters pay by the axle, walkers by the head. It's written on the board, if you can read.
hearth.wild.about.toll_gate.2: Folk swim the ford downstream to save a few bits. Some of them even reach the other side.
hearth.wild.about.hermitage.0: The towns are loud. Out here God speaks quietly, and I have time to listen.
hearth.wild.about.hermitage.1: I had a name once, and a trade. I gave both back. The birds don't mind.
hearth.wild.about.hermitage.2: People come to me with their troubles. I give them herbs and silence. Mostly it is the silence that helps.
hearth.wild.about.hunters_camp.0: Deer, boar when we're lucky. Wolves when they come too close to the flocks. The pelts go to market in the autumn.
hearth.wild.about.hunters_camp.1: The wood edge is where the game is. Deep in, it's all shadow and nothing moves you can eat.
hearth.wild.about.hunters_camp.2: If you see a big grey with a torn ear, that's the one taking the shepherds' lambs. There's coin on her head.
hearth.wild.about.caravan_stop.0: Anyone with a cart and a long way to go. Water, a pen for the beasts, a wall round it all. That's worth a lot out here.
hearth.wild.about.caravan_stop.1: The caravans trade with each other here as much as anywhere. You'd be surprised what changes hands at night.
hearth.wild.about.caravan_stop.2: A train came through from the far side of the hills last week. Salt and cloth, and stories nobody believed.
hearth.wild.about.monastery.0: Pray, copy books, brew, tend the terraces. The days are long up here and none of them are wasted.
hearth.wild.about.monastery.1: Pilgrims climb up on the feast days. Some of them for the relics, most of them for the beer.
hearth.wild.about.monastery.2: Our library has books the bishop's men would burn if they knew we kept them. Don't tell them.
hearth.wild.about.nomad_camp.0: Where the grass is. Two grounds, back and forth with the season. The herd decides more than we do.
hearth.wild.about.nomad_camp.1: Town people think we're lost. We think they're stuck.
hearth.wild.about.nomad_camp.2: In a few days we pack the felts and move on. You'll find us on the other ground if you want horses.
hearth.wild.about.harbour.0: Good when the water's grey, poor when it's bright. Today it's somewhere between.
hearth.wild.about.harbour.1: We take the catch to the nearest market on the cart, salted. Fresh fish doesn't travel.
hearth.wild.about.harbour.2: Old Hanne swears there's something big out past the point that takes the nets. Nobody's seen it. Nets go missing all the same.
hearth.wild.about.farmstead.0: Hard enough. The wind never stops, and the wolves only stop when they're fed. But the wool is the best in the valley.
hearth.wild.about.farmstead.1: The flock is on the hill from spring till the first snow. Then it's all of us and them in the barn till Candlemas.
hearth.wild.about.farmstead.2: You can sleep in the hay if you're caught out. It's warm, and the dog will tell us if you're not honest.
hearth.wild.toll.halt.0: Halt there! Bridge toll, %s, and you pass.
hearth.wild.toll.halt.1: Hold! Nobody crosses here without paying the lord's toll: %s.
hearth.wild.toll.halt.2: Stop a moment, traveller. The toll is %s.
hearth.wild.toll.paid.0: Thank you. Pass, and God speed.
hearth.wild.toll.paid.1: Right. On you go. Mind the third plank, it's loose.
hearth.wild.toll.paid.2: Paid and noted. You'll pass freely till the day's out.
hearth.wild.toll.go_on: So you have. Go on, then.
hearth.wild.toll.talked: ...Oh, go on. But if my master asks, I never saw you.
hearth.wild.toll.refused: Nice try. No coin, no crossing. Lads, stand the gate.
hearth.wild.toll.go_round: Suit yourself. The river's wide and cold. The lads will keep the gate meanwhile.
hearth.wild.toll.evaded.0: Oi! You haven't paid! The reeve will hear of this!
hearth.wild.toll.evaded.1: Toll dodger! Stop! I know your face now!
hearth.wild.toll.evaded.2: Hey! That's the lord's toll you're cheating!
hearth.wild.tend: Could I have something to eat, and my wounds seen to?
hearth.wild.tend.given: Sit. Here is soup, and bread. Let me look at that arm... There. You'll do. Go with God.
hearth.wild.tend.again: We fed you already today, friend. Others are coming over the pass behind you.
hearth.wild.rumour: What have you heard of far places?
hearth.wild.rumour.none: Nothing that would help you. The world is wide, and I keep to my corner of it.
hearth.wild.rumour.town: Travellers speak of %1$s, %3$s leagues to the %2$s. A good place, they say, or a bad one. They always say both.
